name: chroot
description: Runs a command with a different directory as its filesystem root — the foundation of recovery environments and containers.

flags.description: Run COMMAND inside the new root.

examples.explanation: THE recovery pattern: boot a Live USB, mount the broken system's root, chroot into it — now update-grub, passwd, and apt operate on the real system.
Explicitly specifies the shell to run inside the new root.

about: chroot changes only the filesystem root view — it does NOT isolate processes, network, or users (that requires namespaces/containers). The new root must contain everything the command needs: libraries (/lib), devices (/dev via bind mount), and proc (/proc). A typical rescue sequence bind-mounts /dev, /proc, and /sys first.
useCases: Repair unbootable systems from a Live USB.
Build minimal application environments (the ancestor of containers).
mistakes: Chrooting without mounting /proc, /dev, /sys — tools inside fail mysteriously.
Forgetting to copy resolv.conf, so DNS fails inside.
warnings: chroot is NOT a security boundary. Processes inside can still access the network and, as root, escape via file descriptors. Use real containers/namespaces for isolation.
